pr.title: mir-opt: Do not create storage marks in EarlyOtherwiseBranch
pr.description:
Fixes #141212.

The first commit add `StorageDead` by creating new indirect BB that makes CFG more complicated, but I think it's better to just not create storage marks.

r? mir-opt
pr.author: dianqk

issues.title: EarlyOtherwiseBranch can insert storage markers incorrectly, creating use of a dead local

analysis.summary: EarlyOtherwiseBranch was fixed to stop synthesizing StorageLive/StorageDead markers when it hoists a second discriminant comparison. The old code placed StorageDead at statement index 0 of each branch target; when a target was the same block containing the new switchInt (a self-loop), that StorageDead landed before the `switchInt(move _temp)` use, producing a use of a dead local. The fix removes all storage markers for the created temps instead of adding more CFG edges.
analysis.originalLogic: When EarlyOtherwiseBranch hoists the second discriminant into a temp and compares it with the parent discriminant, it creates temps with `patch.new_temp`, emits `StorageLive` before the assignments, and emits `StorageDead` after the comparison and at the start of the branch targets. The PR's old code did: `patch.add_statement(parent_end, StatementKind::StorageLive(second_discriminant_temp));`, `patch.add_statement(parent_end, StatementKind::StorageLive(comp_temp));`, then for each target `patch.add_statement(Location { block: *bb, statement_index: 0 }, StatementKind::StorageDead(comp_temp));`. The title states: "mir-opt: Do not create storage marks in EarlyOtherwiseBranch"; the PR says "The first commit add `StorageDead` by creating new indirect BB that makes CFG more complicated, but I think it's better to just not create storage marks."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation is inserting `StorageDead(comp_temp)` at `statement_index: 0` of each new switchInt target without accounting for a target being the same block as `parent_end`. In the reduced example, bb1 is both the parent block and the `otherwise` target: the pass inserts `StorageDead(_4)` at the start of bb1, before the newly added `_4 = Ne(...)` and `switchInt(move _4)`, so the switchInt reads a dead temp. The issue diff shows `StorageLive(_4);`, `_4 = Ne(copy _1, copy _1);`, `StorageDead(_4);`, then `switchInt(move _4)`. The corrected transformation removes all `StorageLive`/`StorageDead` for `second_discriminant_temp` and `comp_temp`; the new test diff has only `_2 = Ne(copy _1, copy _1);` followed by `switchInt(move _2)`, with no storage markers.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR after earlier optimizations containing nested `match`/`switchInt` on the same place or on discriminants of tuple fields, where EarlyOtherwiseBranch recognizes an early-otherwise pattern and hoists the second discriminant/comparison. The problematic domain includes control flow where one of the replacement switchInt targets is the same block as the block ending in that switchInt (self-referential target), as in the custom-MIR `target_self` test with `match val { 0 => bb2, _ => bb1, }` then `match val { 0 => bb3, _ => bb1, }`.
analysis.trigger: A branch target of the transformed switchInt equals the parent block where the new comparison temp is used, causing the inserted `StorageDead` at `statement_index: 0` of that target to precede the `switchInt(move _temp)`. The issue title is "EarlyOtherwiseBranch can insert storage markers incorrectly, creating use of a dead local"; the reproduction is a `match` whose fallback arm is `_ => bb1` while bb1 is also the block containing the match.
preconditions: EarlyOtherwiseBranch is enabled and matches an early-otherwise pattern that requires hoisting the second discriminant comparison
A new temporary for the comparison is moved into the generated switchInt
One of the generated switchInt targets (true_case/false_case) is the same block as parent_end, i.e. a self-loop target
pitfalls: Do not treat this as a borrow-checking or Tree Borrows issue: the issue notes the unoptimized program is accepted by Miri using Tree Borrows, while the reported failure is 'Undefined Behavior: accessing a dead local variable'.
Do not add StorageLive/StorageDead merely by creating an extra indirect basic block; the accepted fix removes storage markers entirely rather than complicating the CFG, per the PR description.
A retained test name or old comment in the mir-opt diff does not prove the replacement pass is correct; compare actual assignments and storage markers in the decoded before/after MIR.

The relevant wrongness is ordering/placement of StorageDead relative to `switchInt(move _temp)` when a target is the parent block; other properties of the transformed MIR (such as copying vs moving the parent discriminant) are separate.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a `//@ test-mir-pass: EarlyOtherwiseBranch` custom-MIR regression test where one match arm loops back to the same block, e.g. `target_self(val: i32)` with `match val { 0 => bb2, _ => bb1, }` and then `match val { 0 => bb3, _ => bb1, }`. Check the emitted pass MIR for `Ne(` followed by `switchInt` and, crucially, assert that no `StorageLive`/`StorageDead` for the new temp appears in the parent block or target blocks. Alternatively run the reduced program under Miri with `-Zmir-enable-passes=+EarlyOtherwiseBranch` to catch 'accessing a dead local variable'. The supplied test uses `// CHECK: Ne(` / `// CHECK-NEXT: switchInt`, and the new diff shows no storage markers around `_2 = Ne(copy _1, copy _1)`.
